messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Microsatellite Data import
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

The reason this is happening is because the "sep" argument is antagonistic to the "ncode" argument. If you have both sep and ncode, sep will win and obviously gives you incorrect results (the devel version of adegenet will give you a warning if this happens). The answer to the problem you are posting is to specify ncode = 3 and not sep = "". However, if I'm reading this correctly, you are having a problem where your data don't are not strictly 3-coded alleles.

If you have data where you have either 4 or 6 characters to encode alleles, the answer is to add zeros to the beginning of the 2code alleles with the `str_replace_all()` function from the stringr package. The example below shows how you can find an entry that has exactly two digits encoding the data (in the code [0-9]{2} means 2 of any digit, ^ means the beginning of the string element, and $ means the end).

library("stringr")
x <- data.frame(pop = c("A", "B"),
                x = c("1234", "567890"),
                y = c("098765", "4321"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE
               )
x
#>   pop      x      y
#> 1   A   1234 098765
#> 2   B 567890   4321
to_find <- "^([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$"
x[] <- lapply(x, FUN = str_replace_all, to_find, "0\\10\\2")
x
#>   pop      x      y
#> 1   A 012034 098765
#> 2   B 567890 043021

Hope that helps.

Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: Generating SE for basic frequency stats
messages.subject_clean: Generating SE for basic frequency stats
messages.body_plain:
I realize that I sent this to Leah, but not to the group (sorry for the double posting, Leah)

Assuming that you have the 40 values of Ho/He (8 X 5) necessary to calculate the means, you can calculate standard error from the mean by defining the function se <- function(x) sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)) and using that on each column/row of the 8x5 matrix.

Here's an example of extracting the Hexp mean and se for the first five populations of the nancycats data set:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))
data(nancycats)
n5 <- seppop(nancycats, drop = FALSE)[1:5]
Ho <- function(x) summary(x)$Hobs
He <- function(x) locus_table(x, information = FALSE)[seq(nLoc(x)), "Hexp", drop = TRUE]
se <- function(x) sd(x)/length(x)
He_overall<- sapply(n5, FUN = He)
He_overall
#>             P01       P02       P03       P04       P05
#> fca8  0.6416667 0.7875264 0.7753623 0.8115942 0.8091954
#> fca23 0.7210526 0.6300211 0.8768116 0.7864734 0.6850575
#> fca43 0.7789474 0.7008457 0.7500000 0.7207729 0.8160920
#> fca45 0.6789474 0.7505285 0.6884058 0.7159420 0.7885057
#> fca77 0.7842105 0.8636364 0.7898551 0.8096618 0.7678161
#> fca78 0.5263158 0.6617336 0.6739130 0.7903382 0.3931034
#> fca90 0.7263158 0.6987315 0.7862319 0.8289855 0.6620690
#> fca96 0.6263158 0.5465116 0.6992754 0.7285024 0.6482759
#> fca37 0.3578947 0.6712474 0.4311594 0.5555556 0.1931034
He_mean_pop <- colMeans(He_overall)
He_se_pop <- apply(He_overall, MARGIN = 2, FUN = se)
He_by_pop <- data.frame(He = He_mean_pop, se = He_se_pop)
He_by_pop
#>            He         se
#> P01 0.6490741 0.01509212
#> P02 0.7011980 0.01022336
#> P03 0.7190016 0.01387738
#> P04 0.7497585 0.00936519
#> P05 0.6403576 0.02361227

Note that if you want to calculate that by locus instead, you would use rowMeans and MARGIN = 1.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject: Loading plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I would like to interpret my results obtained from the loadingplot . The respective plot was obtained from the DAPC analysis. I want to see the structure of my population according to the sampling location. My data set is a haploid and  dominant.
I would like to find out the scale of the y axis and interpret my loci contribution according to the y axis (loadings). For example, whether there is a cut off value for these loci to be claimed as significant for the genetic variation among sampling locations.  And also I would like to know whether the scale of the y axis depends on the number of loci.

Thanking you

Buddhika

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Loading plot
messages.body_plain:
Hello Buddhika,

DAPC is explicitly part of the {adegenet} package, but I'm happy to help out here. The loadingplot is covered in section 3.4 of the adegenet DAPC manual: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/blob/master/tutorials/tutorial-dapc.pdf

Each axis on your DAPC plot represents a discriminant function that attempts to separate your groups. The y axis of the loading plot shows you what proportion the alleles/loci contributed to one particular DA axis, and they all sum to one. There is no particular cutoff value to declare anything as having significant contribution.

I hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.body_plain:
The data from Aeut comes from Grunwald and Hoheisel 2003: https://apsjournals.apsnet.org/doi/pdf/10.1094/PHYTO-96-1134, but I think the data were obtained from a single primer set.

I believe it should be suitable to concatenate multiple tables as you describe, but I do not have sufficient knowledge of RAPD genotyping to confirm this. Does anyone else in the group have experience with RAPD genotyping and can share their expertise?

Best,
Zhian

> > Assuming that you have the 40 values of Ho/He (8 X 5) necessary to calculate the means, you can calculate standard error from the mean by defining the function se <- function(x) sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)) and using that on each column/row of the 8x5 matrix.
> >
> > Here's an example of extracting the Hexp mean and se for the first five populations of the nancycats data set:
> >
> > suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))
> > data(nancycats)
> > n5 <- seppop(nancycats, drop = FALSE)[1:5]
> > Ho <- function(x) summary(x)$Hobs
> > He <- function(x) locus_table(x, information = FALSE)[seq(nLoc(x)), "Hexp", drop = TRUE]
> > se <- function(x) sd(x)/length(x)
> > He_overall<- sapply(n5, FUN = He)
> > He_overall
> > #>             P01       P02       P03       P04       P05
> > #> fca8  0.6416667 0.7875264 0.7753623 0.8115942 0.8091954
> > #> fca23 0.7210526 0.6300211 0.8768116 0.7864734 0.6850575
> > #> fca43 0.7789474 0.7008457 0.7500000 0.7207729 0.8160920
> > #> fca45 0.6789474 0.7505285 0.6884058 0.7159420 0.7885057
> > #> fca77 0.7842105 0.8636364 0.7898551 0.8096618 0.7678161
> > #> fca78 0.5263158 0.6617336 0.6739130 0.7903382 0.3931034
> > #> fca90 0.7263158 0.6987315 0.7862319 0.8289855 0.6620690
> > #> fca96 0.6263158 0.5465116 0.6992754 0.7285024 0.6482759
> > #> fca37 0.3578947 0.6712474 0.4311594 0.5555556 0.1931034
> > He_mean_pop <- colMeans(He_overall)
> > He_se_pop <- apply(He_overall, MARGIN = 2, FUN = se)
> > He_by_pop <- data.frame(He = He_mean_pop, se = He_se_pop)
> > He_by_pop
> > #>            He         se
> > #> P01 0.6490741 0.01509212
> > #> P02 0.7011980 0.01022336
> > #> P03 0.7190016 0.01387738
> > #> P04 0.7497585 0.00936519
> > #> P05 0.6403576 0.02361227
> >
> >
> > Note that if you want to calculate that by locus instead, you would use rowMeans and MARGIN = 1.
> >
> > Hope that helps,
> > Zhian
> >
> >
> > On Monday, October 21, 2019 at 8:43:28 PM UTC+1, Leah Cobb Lee wrote:
> > >
> > > Hi,
> > >
> > > I'm just trying to report some basic frequency stats for 5 populations (8 loci). Through various functions, I've been able to get mean Ho or He for each locus (over all 5 pops) or mean Ho or He for each pop (over all 8 loci). How can I get the standard error for each of these values?
> > >
> > > Also, is it possible to generate a poppr table that displays values for each locus for each population (locus*pop)?
> > >
> > > Thanks,
> > > Leah

It is me again troubling you with a code in adegenet. I cannot find a group for adegent. So I thought post here and get some advice for my issue.

Error in FUN(newX[, i], ...) : arguments must have same length

Then I changed my file format into different formats like text, excel and csv, also I changed the allele names  (Presence 1, Absence 2, Missing 0 ) but still I could not figure out the problem.

I would be grateful to you, if you could advice me.

Thank you.

Best regards
Buddhika

messages.body_plain:
Hi Buddhika,

This is a bug in snapclust, but I don't know how soon it can be fixed since the maintainer of adegenet is currently in the DRC assisting with the Ebola epidemic at the moment. Additionally, snapclust was developed with codominant markers in mind, so it's not clear what the ramifications of using it on dominant markers would be (though I suspect the effect is NIL).

Best,
Zhian
